corrections.text: The Overview section attributes the '30 new lawsuits' figure to Claims Journal, but the Claims Journal article does not state a number of lawsuits. The figure is confirmed by NPR ('Thirty complaints were filed against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman') and heise online ('30 more lawsuits have been filed against OpenAI'), both of which are cited elsewhere in this article. The fact is accurate; the citation in that sentence was to the wrong outlet.

The article quotes NPR as reporting the safety team's recommendation was 'allegedly overridden by OpenAI's global affairs office led by Chris Lehane.' This is a paraphrase, not a verbatim NPR quote. NPR's actual wording is: 'recommendations to alert police... were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane' and, separately, 'that recommendation was overruled by the company's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Lehane.' The substance is accurate; the quotation marks should not have been used for paraphrased text.

The article summary states OpenAI's 'safety team flagged' the shooter's account and executives 'overrode a referral to police.' Per NPR and Claims Journal, the account was flagged by OpenAI's automated system; the safety/investigations team then reviewed the flagged conversations and recommended a referral to law enforcement, which executives declined to act on before any referral was made. No referral to police was ever made and then reversed.
